questions.prompt: A mirror-loaded pair has \(g_m = 1\ \mathrm{mS}\) on the input devices and \(r_o = 100\ \mathrm{k\Omega}\) for every device. Find the single-ended gain \(v_{out}/v_{id}\) at M2's drain.
questions.explanation: \(A_{DM} = G_mR_{out} = g_m(r_{o2}\parallel r_{o4}) = 1\ \mathrm{mS}\times50\ \mathrm{k\Omega} = 50\) (reader Eq. 16.74). Positive with this output: raising \(v_{i1}\) makes the mirror push more current into the output while M2 pulls less.

questions.prompt: Why replace the two load resistors with a current mirror?
options: The mirror delivers the full differential current to one output, so a single-ended output gets the full gain
To remove the need for a tail source
questions.explanation: With resistors, one output gets half the signal; the mirror adds both halves at one node.

questions.prompt: Short the output to AC ground. With \(g_m = 2\ \mathrm{mS}\) for the input devices, what is the stage's transconductance \(G_m = i_{out}/v_{id}\) in mS?
questions.explanation: Half of \(v_{id}\) drives each side; M1's current is mirrored and adds to M2's change: \(i_{out} = g_mv_{id}\), so \(G_m = g_m = 2\ \mathrm{mS}\) (Eq. 16.72).

questions.explanation: Equal currents and gate voltages make M3 and M4 operate identically; in practice the high-impedance output is set by feedback around the amplifier.

questions.prompt: In a mirror-loaded pair with input common-mode voltage 1.0 V and \(V_T = 0.4\ \mathrm{V}\), what is the lowest output voltage (V) that keeps M2 saturated?
questions.explanation: M2 needs \(V_D \ge V_G - V_T = 1.0 - 0.4 = 0.6\ \mathrm{V}\). The top of the swing is set by the PMOS: \(V_{DD} - |V_{ov4}|\).

questions.prompt: Preview of offsets: why does a mirror-loaded pair have a systematic offset even with perfect matching, if the output sits far from the diode node's voltage?
options: Because the tail current is ideal
Different \(V_{SD}\) on M3 and M4 changes their currents through \(\lambda\)
Because the input devices are NMOS
questions.explanation: The mirror copies exactly only when M4's drain voltage equals M3's.
